rules.title: No-pets clause
rules.explanation_if_violated: Ontario's Residential Tenancies Act says a provision in a tenancy agreement prohibiting animals in or about the residential complex is void. The clause is in the lease, but it has no legal effect.

rules.title: Rent acceleration clause
rules.explanation_if_violated: A provision making the remaining rent (or a specific sum) due because the tenant defaulted on rent or another obligation is void under s. 15.

rules.title: Security or damage deposit
rules.explanation_if_violated: Under s. 105(1), the only security deposit a landlord may collect is a rent deposit under s. 106. Damage, pet and similar deposits fall outside that, and s. 4(1) makes lease terms that are inconsistent with the Act void.

rules.title: Rent deposit amount
rules.explanation_if_violated: A rent deposit can't be more than the lesser of one rent period and one month's rent. This one is larger than one month's rent.
rules.explanation_if_compliant: The rent deposit is within the limit of one month's rent.
rules.exception_note: If rent is paid weekly or for another period shorter than a month, the limit is one rent period, which this check doesn't model.

rules.title: Key deposit
rules.citation: Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, s. 134(1)(a); O. Reg. 516/06, s. 17, item 3
rules.explanation_if_violated: A key, fob or card deposit must be refundable and no more than the expected direct cost of replacing it. This one is larger than the replacement cost stated.
rules.explanation_if_compliant: The key deposit is no more than the stated replacement cost. It must also be refundable.

rules.title: Bounced cheque (NSF) fee
rules.citation: Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, s. 134(1); O. Reg. 516/06, s. 17, items 4-5
rules.explanation_if_violated: A landlord's administration charge for an NSF cheque can't exceed $20. The bank's own NSF charges to the landlord can be passed on separately, but not as a larger flat fee.
rules.explanation_if_compliant: The administration charge is within the $20 limit.

rules.title: Required post-dated cheques or automatic payments
rules.explanation_if_violated: Under s. 108, neither a landlord nor a tenancy agreement can require post-dated cheques, automatic bank debits, or automatic credit card charges for rent. A tenant can choose to pay that way, but the lease can't make it a requirement.

rules.title: Landlord entry notice
rules.explanation_if_violated: For non-emergency entries such as repairs or inspections, s. 27 requires written notice at least 24 hours in advance, stating the reason, the day, and a time between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. This clause allows less notice.
rules.explanation_if_compliant: The notice period meets the 24-hour minimum in s. 27.
rules.exception_note: Section 26 allows entry without written notice in an emergency, with the tenant's consent at the time, and in a few other specific situations.

rules.title: Rent increase notice
rules.explanation_if_violated: A landlord must give at least 90 days' written notice before increasing rent. Under s. 116(4), an increase without the required notice is void.
rules.explanation_if_compliant: The notice period meets the 90-day minimum.

rules.title: Rent increase frequency
rules.explanation_if_violated: Rent can be increased only if at least 12 months have passed since the last increase, or since the tenant first rented the unit. This clause allows increases more often.
rules.explanation_if_compliant: The increase frequency respects the 12-month rule.
rules.exception_note: Many units are also subject to the annual rent increase guideline in s. 120, which this check doesn't cover.
